title: Outgoing webhook delivery with retries and signatures
tasks: webhook delivery with retries and signatures

requirements.text: Each delivery is signed with an HMAC over a timestamp and the exact body using the endpoint's secret
Failed deliveries (network errors, timeouts, non-2xx) are retried with exponential backoff, then marked dead after a maximum and can be replayed manually
Pending deliveries are persisted in the same transaction as the triggering change and survive process restarts
Each attempt has a timeout so a slow endpoint cannot hold a worker
Every delivery carries a unique event id that stays the same across retries so receivers can deduplicate
Endpoint URLs must be HTTPS and resolve to public addresses; redirects to internal hosts are not followed
Only authorized tenant members can register endpoints and view or rotate their secrets

evidence.name: worker delivers the exact stored body with a signature verified by the webhook-verification module
secret rotation signs with every active secret until the old one expires
network errors, timeouts and non-2xx responses are retried with backoff and the same webhook-id, then dead
manual replay of a dead delivery requeues it with the same webhook-id and a fresh attempt budget
schema applies and delivery rows commit or roll back with the triggering change on the caller transaction
claim holds until the lease expires, then another worker reclaims it; the stale worker cannot complete
each attempt gets its own AbortSignal timeout; a hung endpoint is aborted and retried
enqueue creates one delivery per (event, endpoint), idempotent on the event id, filtered by event type
network errors, timeouts and non-2xx responses are retried with backoff and the same webhook-id, then dead
isPublicIp and parseIp reject private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, multicast, ULA, mapped and metadata ranges
checkWebhookUrl requires https, refuses credentials, localhost names and non-canonical IPv4 forms
registration refuses URLs that fail the SSRF guard, including hostnames resolving to private addresses
send time re-resolves the host: a hostname rebound to a private address is blocked and not fetched
redirects are not followed: fetch uses redirect manual and a 3xx is a failed attempt
endpoint CRUD and secret rotation call authorize(actor, tenantId, action) and refuse unauthorized actors
tenants cannot read, change, rotate, replay or receive another tenant
HTTP adapter: create shows the secret once, list and get never do, rotate shows the new secret once

implementations.notes: The SSRF guard checks the resolved addresses at registration and at send time and passes them to fetch; closing the DNS-rebinding window needs a fetch that connects to those addresses (for example an undici Agent with a fixed lookup), which the app supplies. PGlite concurrency tests run on one connection.

evidence.name: webhook-signature: Stripe-style header vector and verification failures
outbox commits state and messages atomically and relays at least once

implementations.notes: In-memory outbox: retry with backoff, dead state and revive are tested; it is not durable across restarts

evidence.name: attemptTimeoutMs times out a hung attempt and retries it

implementations.notes: pg-boss queue with retries and a dead-letter queue; enqueuing in the same transaction as the change is the application's work

notes: module:webhook-delivery covers signing, retries with backoff and dead letters, a transactional queue with leases, per-attempt timeouts, stable event ids, an SSRF guard and tenant-scoped endpoint management. The app supplies the transport that pins resolved addresses and its authorization rules.
